name: The deck's retention figure is measured on a denominator the benchmark does not use
description: An anchoring case. The deck reports 131% NRR 'among customers past their first renewal' — phrasing that reads as precision rather than as a caveat — and then compares it to published vertical SaaS benchmarks. The corpus says those benchmarks are all-customer, and that a post-renewal cohort typically reports 25-40 points higher for the same business [S1], with first-year churn of 30-35% concentrated before the first renewal [S2]. The comparable figure is therefore ordinary. The case also contains a claim the deck gets RIGHT — 22,000 groups at $62k giving a $1.4B market, against a corpus range of 21,000-23,000 [S3] — so an analysis that reflexively contradicts everything cannot pass.

claims.rationale: 131% on a post-renewal cohort is not comparable to all-customer benchmarks of 104-112% [S1]. Treating it as outperformance is the anchoring failure: the deck supplied the denominator and the reader kept it.

The corpus gives 21,000-23,000 groups [S3], so the deck's count and the arithmetic built on it are sound. Marking this contradicted would show the analysis is pattern-matching on 'deck claims are inflated'.

blind_spots.rationale: The churn the stated denominator excludes, which is where it all happens.
The specific reason the deck's figure cannot be read against the benchmark.
The buyer count is shrinking 3-4% a year; the deck's market is static.
